verses.text: Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before that Pharaoh struck Gaza.

Yahweh says: “Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and will become an overflowing stream, and will overflow the land and all that is therein, the city and those who dwell therein. The men will cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall wail.
At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong ones, at the rushing of his chariots, at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers don’t look back to their children for feebleness of hands;
because of the day that comes to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every helper who remains; for Yahweh will destroy the Philistines, the remnant of the isle of Caphtor.
Baldness has come on Gaza; Ashkelon is brought to nothing, the remnant of their valley: how long will you cut yourself?
“‘You sword of Yahweh, how long will it be before you are quiet? Put yourself back into your scabbard; rest, and be still.’
“How can you be quiet, since Yahweh has given you a command? Against Ashkelon, and against the seashore, there has he appointed it.”

footnotes.content: A word comes before the storm—that's the Lord's mercy, always a warning first. Notice Jeremiah hears it directly from the Almighty; the prophet stands in the counsel of God even when the news is hard. We see the same love in the Savior warning Jerusalem before its fall.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Waters from the north—in Scripture, often a picture of invasion, judgment flowing like a flood. The Philistines, those old enemies of Israel, cannot escape the tide that Yahweh sends. Even those who dwell secure will cry out when God sets His hand in motion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fathers too paralyzed to reach for their own children—that's the terror of it, when human love itself freezes before the sight of disaster. Only the Lord stands unmoved in such moments. We are pressed to see that our strength fails, but His never does.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tyre and Sidon, Gaza, Ashkelon—these great trading cities thought themselves untouchable. But Yahweh's judgment reaches even the proud merchant princes and their helpers. The Lord settles accounts with the nations that have hardened their hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Baldness was a sign of mourning and shame—not vanity lost, but dignity stripped away. Gaza's splendor becomes emptiness; Ashkelon is silenced. When we forget that pride goes before a fall, the Lord reminds us through the fall of nations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophet speaks to the sword as if it could reason—almost pleading for mercy. It's a tender moment, showing Jeremiah's heart even in announcing ruin. Yet the prayer is not heard; the sword will do its work, because God has decreed it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo here: we cannot silence what the Lord has commanded. The blade swings not of its own will but by His appointment. In Christ, we learn that the final Word spoken over all nations is not judgment alone, but redemption for those who turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
